name: England under Edward I, with the monasteries
blurb: Watermills and windmills everywhere, a real legal system, chartered towns, universities, the horse collar, the crank, the mechanical clock arriving, and about to be hit by the worst demographic catastrophe in European history. This variant adds the monastic houses as landlords, millers and lenders. Needs `mod-allow bh_religion_h5p1` for the house to exist.

cast.actors.name: the monastic houses
cast.actors.source: Church land at Domesday was about a quarter of the value of England (Darby, Domesday England, 1977), a share the monasteries held much of by 1300; houses and religious: Knowles and Hadcock, Medieval Religious Houses: England and Wales (1971). Monastic and other seigneurial mills and the customary multure of about a sixteenth of the grain: Langdon, Mills in the Medieval Economy: England 1300-1540 (2004). The mill share is a guess of the right order (heuristic); the land and headcount are placeholders on top of the shipped church entry, not counts.
cast.actors._heuristic: land_share_of_surplus is the share of a year's surplus the house spends on land and land_ceiling_hectares the most it will hold (three times its start, a guess); a stand-in until donors, the house's own rule and the land market's offers are modelled actors (Complaints/636).
